key_insight: Helios is a 14B video-generation model that achieves minute-scale, high-quality videos at real-time speed (19.5 FPS) on a single NVIDIA H100 by eliminating common anti-drifting heuristics and standard acceleration tricks while retaining baseline-quality outputs.
problem_solved: Brings together long-duration stability and real-time throughput for generative video: preventing temporal drift over minutes without heuristic fixes, while delivering interactive-speed generation on a single high-end GPU.
method: Model + training design focused on long-term temporal consistency to avoid drift without self-forcing, error banks, or keyframe sampling.
System and implementation optimizations tailored for a single NVIDIA H100 that enable 19.5 FPS inference for minute-scale videos without relying on KV-cache or sparse/linear attention.
Careful evaluation and scaling (14B parameter regime) to match the quality of strong baselines while meeting throughput and stability targets.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate minute-scale video content in real time on a single GPU while preserving quality, reducing the need for complex heuristics and multi-GPU setups—lowering cost and engineering complexity for production deployments and research.
visual_elements: Sidebar stat block: model size (14B), throughput (19.5 FPS), hardware (NVIDIA H100), duration supported (minute-scale).

Sequence strip showing temporal stability: frame samples over time demonstrating low drift across minutes.
Architecture/stack diagram: training strategies for temporal consistency + system-level optimizations on H100 (icons for model, GPU, and throughput).
paper_title: Helios: Real Real-Time Long Video Generation Model
paper_authors: Shenghai Yuan, Yuanyang Yin, Zongjian Li, Xinwei Huang, Xiao Yang
